newsitem.title: TURKMENISTAN: Turkmens expect $80 mln in two EBRD loans.
newsitem.headline: Turkmens expect $80 mln in two EBRD loans.

text.p: The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) is close to granting Turkmenistan loans worth around $80 million to help upgrade its transport system, a government official told Reuters.

"This refers to the modernisation of the (Caspian) sea port in the town of Turkmenbashi and the upgrading of the Ashgabat-Mary highway," said the official who declined to be named. "Both are part of a project aimed at developing local transport networks," he added.
He said the feasibility study for the modernisation of the sea port had been carried out by U.S. company Louis Berger.
The contractor for construction works in the port will be chosen once a $30 million credit line has been opened. The loan is being granted for 14 years, the official said.

He said the cost of the motorway from the Turkmen capital Ashgabat to the town of Mary 400 km (250 miles) to the north-east would cost another $50 million. The conditions of the loan are still to be defined.
The government of the Central Asian state hopes both projects will be implemented by the year 2000.
The official said the EBRD was currently studying opportunities for investment in Turkmenistan's railways, oil and gas sector, textiles and small and medium-sized businesses.
